### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/scenarios`, touching **20** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/cli.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**7** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/data-api.mdx`  _(via /:object/export (route, bridged from symbol templateMode — its route source's handler names it))_
- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via /:object/export (route, bridged from symbol templateMode — its route source's handler names it))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/cli.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **68** of **250** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **1** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3a81fb7586c175330bd6338a6d1b6abf7d39e6eb` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `aebbba4a5ecb0685d5f61c414db800811b1ad2dc` — the merge of head `6a9b1bd17d34b893ab05862110306cee604bfebe` into base `3a81fb7586c175330bd6338a6d1b6abf7d39e6eb`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin aebbba4a5ecb0685d5f61c414db800811b1ad2dc && git checkout aebbba4a5ecb0685d5f61c414db800811b1ad2dc
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3a81fb7586c175330bd6338a6d1b6abf7d39e6eb 6a9b1bd17d34b893ab05862110306cee604bfebe && git checkout -B drift-repro 3a81fb7586c175330bd6338a6d1b6abf7d39e6eb && git merge --no-ff 6a9b1bd17d34b893ab05862110306cee604bfebe

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3a81fb7586c175330bd6338a6d1b6abf7d39e6eb
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 3a81fb7586c175330bd6338a6d1b6abf7d39e6eb` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `6a9b1bd17d34b893ab05862110306cee604bfebe`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/qa/scenarios/src/score/scenario-run-grade.ts, packages/qa/scenarios/src/score/index.ts, packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/orchestrate.ts, packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/cli.ts, packages/qa/scenarios/src/export/transcript.ts
Security-touching: no

Owed on the `Clause-②: yes (widening)` declaration alone (no `packages/spec/src/**`, no governed path): the lane seat's in-seat review at `TIER_DEFAULT`, as on #36320.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Public surface widened, optional inputs only. Right.** `PersonaRunInput.schemaMasking?: 'on' | 'off'` (`./score`, `./score/full`), `CardAnswer.schemaMasking?: 'on' | 'off'` (`./score/full`), `RunOptions.schemaMasking?: SchemaMasking` and a new last optional parameter on `runHalf` (`./runner`). No export removed, renamed or narrowed; every new field is spread only when set, so an existing caller's grade input is byte for byte unchanged.
- **Grading accept set: narrowed only on the opt-out round. Right.** `declinesWithheld` keeps `ASKER_DECLINE` and `WITHHELD_ACT` on both modes; `UNRECORDED` and the new `UNTRACKED` (moved out of `ASKER_DECLINE_EN`) count only when `schemaMasking === 'on'`. Default masking reads exactly the set it read before (`ASKER_DECLINE ∪ UNTRACKED ∪ UNRECORDED ∪ WITHHELD_ACT`). `DECLINE` gains `UNTRACKED_EN` in its alternation, so `declines()` (the `unanswerable` grade) matches the same strings as before.
- **Masking is read from the record, never the exporter. Right.** `buildTranscript` re-grades under `record.env.schemaMasking === 'off'`; `ScenarioRunRecordSchema` is unchanged. Ablation 3 turns the transcript case red, so a masking-off record is not re-graded under the exporter's environment.
- **Grade module stays runner-free. Right.** `SchemaMaskingMode` is spelled locally in `scenario-run-grade.ts`; only `orchestrate.ts` imports the runner's `SchemaMasking` type.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/36329-masking-off-field-absence.md`: `@objectstack/scenarios` patch; `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch`, matching. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are line-initial in body and changeset, and the changeset names every new input.

### ③ Boundary flags

None. The one-line `cli.ts` hand-off is not pinned by a test (stated in the PR); it passes the same `schemaMasking` value the record stamps on the next line.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-36329-masking-off-field-absence`
Reviewed-by: `session_01ADHkmRY38EZf38Yy3zthbY`

No must-fix, no should-fix.

**VERDICT: PASS**
